role: Building control surveyor reviewing a single stage inspection record before deciding whether the builder may proceed to the next notifiable stage
setting: A building control team inspects new-build and extension work at statutory stages (foundations, damp-proof course, drainage, frame, insulation, pre-plaster, completion). After each site visit an inspection record is compiled from the project file, the approved specification, the surveyor's site readings, the defect list, uploaded evidence and the builder's progress log. A reviewing surveyor reads one record at a time and decides whether the stage can be signed off, how serious any open defects are, and whether key claims about sequence and conformity are supported.

inspected_before_cover.instructions: The stage was inspected before follow-on work covered it.

criteria.true: Inspection date clearly precedes any logged covering work.
criteria.false: Covered first, same-day order unclear, or dates missing.

matches_spec.instructions: Measured as-built details match the approved specification for this stage.

next_step.instructions: What should happen next with this stage inspection?

criteria.sign_off: Stage compliant, fully evidenced; builder proceeds without any conditions.
criteria.conditional_pass: Only workmanship items open, evidence complete; check at next visit.
criteria.hold: No regulatory defect, but one certificate or confirmation awaited.
criteria.reinspect: Regulatory defect or early cover-up; revisit before work proceeds.

defect_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst defect still open at this stage?
criteria: None: no open defect recorded against this stage
Workmanship: open items all tagged workmanship, no regulation area
Regulatory: worst open item tagged energy, ventilation or drainage
Life_safety: any open item tagged structure or fire

pending_age.instructions: How long has this record been waiting without any decision?
criteria: Waiting between one and seven days
Waiting between eight and thirty days
Waiting more than thirty days without decision

factors.name: stage_type
factors.description: Which notifiable stage the visit covered; changes which spec values, tests and covering events are relevant.

factors.name: cover_sequence
factors.description: Order of inspection versus the builder's logged covering event (concrete poured, trench backfilled, boards fixed, plaster started).

factors.name: spec_deviation
factors.description: How the surveyor's measured values differ from the approved specification for the stage.

factors.name: tolerance_boundary
factors.description: A measured value sits exactly on the stated tolerance limit, leaving conformity arguable.

factors.name: engineer_letter
factors.description: An engineer's or designer's letter accepting the as-built change is uploaded; mitigates structural or product deviations.

factors.name: variation_status
factors.description: Status of an amended-plan variation covering the deviation, if any.

factors.name: worst_open_defect
factors.description: Regulation area of the most serious defect genuinely still open at this stage.

factors.name: closed_status_conflict
factors.description: A defect marked closed in the list is described as still outstanding in a free-text note, or vice versa.

factors.name: evidence_gap
factors.description: What supporting evidence is missing for the stage.

factors.name: identifier_mismatch
factors.description: Plot or project reference on the inspection differs from the project section.

factors.name: prior_failed_visits
factors.description: Count of earlier failed or aborted visits for this same stage in the history list.

factors.name: note_hedging
factors.description: Surveyor note uses hedged wording about what could actually be seen, weakening any conformity claim.

sections.name: project
sections.description: Project ref, plot number, work type, plan approval status and any variation with its status.

sections.name: approved_spec
sections.description: Key approved values for the stage, e.g. depth_mm, insulation_mm, product, pipe_dia_mm, tolerance_mm.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Visit date, stage, plot_ref, surveyor id, measured values with units, and free-text surveyor_note.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of items with id, reg_area tag, status open/closed, raised date and a one-line note.

sections.name: evidence
sections.description: Photo count and dates, test certificates with status, engineer letter, builder_message; may be null.

sections.name: site_progress
sections.description: Builder's logged covering events with dates and list of previous visits for this stage with results.

rendering_notes: stage_type sets inspection.stage and decides which approved_spec fields and site_progress cover event appear (foundations: concrete_poured; drainage: backfilled plus air_test cert; insulation: boards_fixed; pre_plaster: plaster_started). cover_sequence appears only through comparing inspection.visit_date with site_progress.cover_events[].date: same_day_ambiguous gives equal dates with no times; cover_date_missing gives date null or the event absent. spec_deviation is shown by inspection.measured values against approved_spec: unit_only renders e.g. 0.15 m against 150 mm (conforming); within_tolerance stays inside approved_spec.tolerance_mm; material_shortfall falls below it; wrong_product names a different product string in measured.product. tolerance_boundary puts the reading exactly on the limit. engineer_letter appears as evidence.engineer_letter {date, scope} or null; variation_status as project.variation {ref, status} or null; a pending variation does not make a deviation conform. worst_open_defect is rendered through defects[] reg_area tags (workmanship, energy, ventilation, drainage, structure, fire) and status; closed_status_conflict marks an item closed while its note or the surveyor_note says it was not rectified, so the true open set must be inferred. evidence_gap: test_cert_pending gives a certificate with status awaiting; photos_absent gives photo_count 0; evidence_section_null makes the whole evidence section null. identifier_mismatch alters inspection.plot_ref against project.plot (typo: transposed digit). prior_failed_visits fills site_progress.previous_visits with result fail or aborted. note_hedging adds phrases like 'appeared to be' or 'partly obscured by spoil' to surveyor_note. Decoys: evidence.builder_message always sounds confident ('all done to drawings'), photo dates may precede the visit, defects of other stages may appear with status closed, and a high photo count never proves conformity. Records never contain an outcome, sign-off, severity, risk or compliance field; no field states whether work was covered early or matches spec.
